title: Measuring Left Ventricular Pressure in Late Embryonic and Neonatal Mice
protocol: Start the ultrasound system according to manufacturer's instructions.
Fill the appropriate probe with distilled water and connect it to the ultrasound system.
Place the probe in the adjustable stand for an LV long-axis view of a mouse mounted on the imaging platform.
Calibrate the pressure transducer system with a manometer.
Mount the needle tubing and casing in the injection arm of the ultrasound system.
Clamp the pressure transducer in a ring stand at the approximate height of the imaging platform.
Attach a needle appropriate for the age of the mouse to the needle tubing.
Place a mound of ultrasound gel on the imaging platform.
Line up the probe using the adjustable stand so that the needle can be advanced directly into the gel under the center of the imaging probe.
Retract the needle and raise the imaging probe to place a mouse on the imaging platform.
Flush the needle to eliminate any gel that may have entered the tip.
Anesthetize a timed pregnant mother or neonatal mouse by continuous inhalation of 1.5% isoflurane.
Secure the mouse to the imaging platform of the ultrasound system in a dorsal decubitus position.
Apply ultrasound gel to monitor heart rate with the attached ECG detector for pregnant mothers.
Insert the rectal thermometer for feedback control of body temperature for pregnant mothers.
Maintain body temperature with an external heat lamp for neonatal mice.
Remove hair from the abdomen of pregnant mothers or chest of young mice with a depilatory cream.
Cut open the abdomen using dissecting scissors and curved forceps for pregnant mothers.
Externalize one uterine horn and place on gauze moistened with warm saline solution.
Manipulate an embryo into the proper position to obtain a parasternal long axis view of the LV using the ultrasound probe.
Measure pressure in all embryos on this side before externalizing the other uterine horn.
Keep all embryos and the abdomen of the mother moist with periodic addition of warm saline.
Place prewarmed, degassed ultrasound gel on the embryonic or neonatal mouse.
Rub a small amount of ultrasound gel onto the chest of non-depilated neonatal mice before applying the remaining ultrasound gel to enhance coupling.
Lower the imaging probe and adjust the angle of the imaging platform to obtain an optimal parasternal LV long axis view.
Do not adjust the angle of the probe because the needle alignment will be lost.
Monitor the LV image on the ultrasound screen while advancing the needle until it is near the bottom of the probe.
Adjust the needle and probe position, if necessary, to correct alignment shifts.
Gently flush the needle with saline.
Start recording pressure data.
Zero the pressure transducer with LabChart software.
Advance the needle until it can be seen at the edge of the ultrasound image but not yet in the LV.
Adjust the needle position, if necessary, to enter the LV at the apex.
Adjust the probe position, if necessary, to maintain a clear image of the needle.
Advance the needle into the LV lumen while recording pressure data and monitoring the needle location on the ultrasound image.
The start of pulsatile recordings from the pressure transducer confirms the location inside the LV lumen.
Flush the needle with a light tap on the syringe plunger if pressure recordings are not pulsatile.
Retract and flush the needle with saline if pressure readings are still not pulsatile after flushing.
Use a new needle for each mouse if pulsatile readings cannot be obtained.
Exclude heart rate data from analysis if it is significantly different than expected.
